topIssues.title: kona-interop: Review access of blocks created internally
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
Currently when Kona-proofs interop performs the interop validation step, if the first validation pass identifies blocks that need to be replaced, it builds them and sets them as chain head then does another validation pass to see if that has caused other chains to become invalid.  But in the second pass it loads the deposit-only block it just generated from the preimage oracle. This block will be canonical so the load will work, but given the block was just built this is a suspicious design choice.

If it ever asks the preimage oracle from a block that isn't canonical (eg an optimistic block it just derived which is later replaced), it would cause failures.  We should review for safety and consider prioritising first checking if the block is already known before loading from the oracle.

topPRs.title: chore(contracts): add non-idempotent initializer review rules
topPRs.author: smartcontracts
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Populates the empty `docs/ai/contract-dev.md` with a "Non-Idempotent Initializers" review guideline for AI agents
- Adds a matching rule to the Graphite/Diamond code review rules (`ops/ai-eng/graphite/rules.md`)

Addresses audit finding #20: potential footgun when re-initializing `ETHLockbox` with only its own `OptimismPortal`. The triage decision was to add review rules (not contract code changes) to catch this class of issue — `initialize()` functions that are not safe to re-run because they increment counters, append to arrays, make non-idempotent external calls, or overwrite variables that other systems depend on.

## Test plan

- [x] Verify `docs/ai/contract-dev.md` replaces the TODO with actionable review guidance
- [x] Verify `ops/ai-eng/graphite/rules.md` includes the new rule section with warning template
- [ ] Confirm Diamond picks up the new rule on future PRs touching `initialize()` functions
